job.title: Finance Manager
job.description:
The Opportunity.
In this role, you’ll take ownership of key areas of the reporting cycle, working across multiple entities to ensure accurate and timely financial information. You’ll bring strong technical accounting expertise, support robust financial controls and help identify opportunities to improve how we operate.
You’ll also work closely with colleagues across Finance and the wider business, providing insight and guidance on financial matters and helping to ensure we have the right processes in place to support effective decision-making.

What You’ll Be Doing.

  • Support the Month-End: Play a key role in the month-end close alongside the Group Reporting team, owning accruals, prepayments and balance sheet reconciliations for your areas, ensuring accuracy and timeliness.
  • Lead Accounts Payable: Own the end-to-end accounts payable process, from supplier onboarding and invoice processing to payment runs, ensuring suppliers are paid accurately and on time with robust controls in place.
  • Own Project Accounting: Track the financial performance of specific initiatives, ensuring costs are captured, allocated and reported correctly, and providing clear insight to project stakeholders.
  • Manage Travel & Expenses: Oversee travel spend and the travel and expense systems used across the business, maintaining clear policies, driving compliance and identifying opportunities to control costs.
  • Strengthen Our Treasury Function: Contribute to the treasury function by building and maintaining cash flow models, producing cash reporting and forecasts, and managing our day-to-day banking relationships.


What You’ll Bring.

  • A professional accounting qualification (CIMA, ACCA or equivalent)
  • Proven experience in an operational finance role, with hands-on ownership of accounts payable, cash management and month-end processes.
  • Hands-on experience building cash flow models and forecasts, and working directly with banking partners.
  • Advanced Excel capabilities and experience tracking and reporting spend at a project or initiative level.
  • Experience managing and developing people and resources within an operational finance team, with excellent communication skills and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment.

Bonus Points If You Have:

  • Industry experience within a high-growth tech or SaaS company.
  • Experience implementing or managing travel and expense systems (e.g. Ramp, Navan or similar).
  • Hands-on experience with ERP systems like NetSuite.
  • A track record of automating and improving AP, treasury or expense processes.

job.title: Financial Accountant
job.description:
About the company
Our client is a fast-growing, values-led FMCG business producing high-quality consumer products with a strong, well-loved brand. Having scaled rapidly in recent years, the business is now strengthening its in-house finance function to support the next stage of growth.
The culture is fast-paced, collaborative and transparent, with a close-knit team that pitches in to help one another. This is an opportunity to join a business on an exciting growth journey and make a visible impact on how it operates.

Key responsibilities

  • Take ownership of day-to-day financial accounting within a fully in-house finance team
  • Provide technical accounting expertise and support to the Head of Finance and Finance Director
  • Manage the month-end and year-end close processes, including reconciliations, journals and accruals
  • Prepare accurate management and statutory accounts
  • Support the annual audit process and act as a key point of contact for auditors
  • Investigate financial issues, develop practical solutions and work with stakeholders to agree the approach
  • Review and improve finance processes, controls and KPIs as the business formalises after a period of rapid growth
  • Contribute to the review of finance systems to ensure they remain fit for purpose as the business scales
  • Support and guide the Finance Assistant and part-time finance staff
  • Respond flexibly to changing business priorities and ad hoc requests from across the business

Requirements

  • Newly qualified, or part-qualified with strong relevant experience
  • Strong technical accounting knowledge, with a focus on financial rather than commercial accounting
  • Experience working in an in-house finance function, ideally within FMCG, consumer goods or manufacturing
  • Exposure to the audit process
  • A practical, hands-on approach: comfortable rolling up your sleeves and owning the detail
  • Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate issues and propose solutions
  • Highly adaptable and comfortable in a fast-paced environment with shifting priorities
  • Collaborative, approachable and keen to be a visible, engaged member of the team
  • Willingness to work on-site

job.title: Financial Controller
job.description:
About the role
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Financial Controller to join a fast-growing, multi-site hospitality business.
Reporting to the Head of Finance, you’ll lead a team of five and take ownership of financial reporting, controls and process improvement. This is a hands-on role with plenty of opportunity to improve how the finance function operates as the business continues to scale.

Responsibilities

  • Lead, coach and develop a finance team of five.
  • Own and improve the period-end close process.
  • Oversee management accounts, balance sheet reconciliations and financial controls.
  • Manage site-level controls across stock, GP, cash and payroll.
  • Lead the year-end audit and statutory reporting process.
  • Improve and automate finance processes.
  • Partner with the wider business to support continued growth and new site openings.

Requirements

  • Qualified accountant: ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent.
  • 5+ years’ post-qualified experience.
  • Previous Financial Controller or Finance Manager experience.
  • Ideally from multi-site hospitality, leisure, retail or a similar consumer-facing business.
  • Strong management accounting, controls and Excel experience.
  • Experience managing and developing a finance team.
  • Hands-on, proactive and comfortable improving processes in a growing environment.

Why join?
A great opportunity to join a growing consumer business where you can make a genuine impact, build out processes and controls, and develop a strong finance team

job.title: Finance Transformation Lead
job.description:
The Business
A fastgrowing, international technology business operating across multiple entities and jurisdictions. As the company continues to scale globally, they are investing in their finance function to improve processes, systems, controls and reporting.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead finance transformation initiatives across processes, systems, controls and data.
  • Review and redesign core finance processes to improve efficiency, scalability and control.
  • Lead finance systems and automation projects from requirements through to implementation.
  • Improve the financial close, reconciliations, journal management, reporting and consolidation processes.
  • Develop stronger data governance and reporting frameworks, creating a reliable single source of truth.
  • Identify process inefficiencies and control gaps, implementing practical improvements.
  • Partner with Finance, Technology and wider business teams to deliver transformation projects.
  • Support the development of the future Finance Target Operating Model.
  • Drive successful adoption of new systems and ways of working across the finance team.


Key Requirements

  • Qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent).
  • Strong technical accounting background with experience operating at Financial Controller / Head of Finance level.
  • Experience within a complex, multi-entity and ideally international environment.
  • Strong knowledge across month-end close, reconciliations, consolidation, intercompany accounting and statutory reporting.
  • Proven experience leading finance transformation, systems implementation or process improvement projects.
  • Experience with ERP, finance automation or EPM tools.
  • Comfortable combining hands-on finance knowledge with systems, process and transformation expertise.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to work across Finance, Technology and senior leadership.
  • Experience within a fast-growth technology or SaaS environment would be beneficial.

job.title: Finance Manager
job.description:
About the business
We’re partnering with a fast-growing, international B2B SaaS business looking to hire a Finance Manager into a pivotal role within its finance team.
Operating across multiple international markets, the business is at an exciting stage of growth and is now looking to bring more of its finance function in-house. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys a broad, hands-on role and wants to help build and shape a finance function as the company scales.

The role
Reporting directly to the CFO, you’ll be the senior day-to-day finance person for the UK, taking ownership of UK finance operations as well as supporting group reporting and consolidation.
A major focus will be bringing finance processes in-house, improving controls and helping develop the systems and processes needed to support future growth.

Key responsibilities

  • Lead the transition of the finance function in-house
  • Own the monthly close and preparation of UK management accounts
  • Prepare multi-entity, multi-currency group consolidations
  • Manage FX, intercompany accounting and eliminations
  • Design and improve finance processes, controls and systems
  • Take ownership of AP, payment runs and supplier reconciliations
  • Coordinate year-end and work closely with external accountants and tax advisers
  • Ensure compliance with UK GAAP and/or IFRS
  • Provide accurate financial information to support FP&A, budgeting and forecasting
  • Work closely with overseas finance teams/accountants
  • ACA / ACCA qualified, or approaching final qualification
  • Strong hands-on management accounting experience
  • Experience within a multi-entity or international group
  • Strong consolidation, FX and intercompany accounting knowledge
  • Comfortable operating across both transactional and technical finance
  • Ideally experienced in a SaaS, technology, PE-backed or fast-growth SME environment
  • Previous experience bringing finance in-house, transforming processes or implementing new systems would be highly advantageous
  • A proactive, hands-on personality with the confidence to work directly with senior leadership

job.title: Group FP&A Manager
job.description:
The business
Our client is an independent, award-winning global media, creative and data agency that works with some of the world's best-known brands. It's growing quickly, both organically and through acquisitions, and has offices in the UK and US. Right now it's changing its operating model and modernising its finance systems, so this is a chance to shape a finance function while it's being rebuilt. The business is regularly recognised as a great place to work.

The role
You'll report to the Head of Group FP&A and work closely with the CFO, the C-suite, Operations and the agency leads in both the UK and US. You'll help move finance away from manual legacy processes to automated, scalable ways of working.

Responsibilities

  • Work closely with the CFO, senior leadership and division heads across the UK and US media and creative businesses
  • Turn complex financial data into clear stories and recommendations for executive decisions
  • Co-lead the annual budget, quarterly reforecasts and long-range planning, acting as the central FP&A contact
  • Build financial models, scenarios and sensitivity analysis for business cases, expansion and capital allocation
  • Produce monthly Board packs, executive dashboards and variance commentary
  • Support M&A activity, including due diligence, integrating models for acquired businesses and reporting to PE investors
  • Work with Operations and senior leaders to model and deliver a group-wide operating model change
  • Review pricing models, pitch economics, third-party costs and capacity across service lines
  • Help review and design bonus, commission and performance incentive schemes
  • Find manual bottlenecks in planning and reporting and replace them with automated solutions, using AI where it fits8
  • Represent FP&A in designing, testing and rolling out a new ERP and planning tool
  • Work with the BI and Data teams to improve data flows and build scalable reporting


Requirements

  • ACA, ACCA, CIMA or an equivalent qualification
  • A degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics or a related subject
  • 4+ years in FP&A or Commercial Finance, ideally at an agency, in digital marketing or at a PE-backed tech-enabled services business
  • Hands-on experience implementing an ERP or FP&A tool, and a strong interest in automation
  • Excellent financial modelling in Excel or Google Sheets; experience with Looker, Tableau, Power BI or SQL is a strong plus
  • A track record of working across international offices (UK and US especially) and partnering with senior management
  • Comfortable bringing structure to a fast-changing, historically manual environment
  • Strong commercial sense and the confidence to challenge senior stakeholders constructively

job.title: Finance and Operations Manager
job.description:
The business
Our client is an established, founder-led luxury brand headquartered in London. It sells through its own London boutiques, an international store, concessions in leading department stores, wholesale partners and a growing e-commerce channel.
The business is entering its next phase of growth and needs a hands-on finance leader to bring structure, insight and control to finance and operations.

The role
The Finance & Operations Manager owns the end-to-end finance function, from transactions through to management reporting and year end. Reporting to the CFO, you will support the leadership team and the link between finance, retail, e-commerce, wholesale and supply chain. This is a hands-on role in a small team, suited to someone who enjoys both the detail and the bigger picture.

Key responsibilities
Financial management and reporting

  • Run the full month-end close and produce timely, accurate monthly management accounts
  • Prepare board and founder reporting packs with clear commentary on performance, margins and KPIs
  • Own balance sheet reconciliations, accruals, prepayments and the fixed asset register
  • Manage the year-end process and audit, acting as the main contact for external accountants and auditors
  • Oversee statutory compliance, including VAT returns, corporation tax support and Companies House filings

Budgeting, forecasting and commercial insight

  • Lead the annual budget and rolling forecasts with the founder and department heads
  • Build and maintain 13-week cash flow forecasts and manage working capital closely
  • Analyse performance by channel (boutiques, concessions, wholesale, e-commerce) and by product
  • Provide margin, pricing and gross profit analysis, including the impact of metal prices and FX
  • Support business cases for new stores, collections, markets and investment decisions

Retail and operations support

  • Partner with retail and e-commerce teams on store P&Ls, sales reporting, footfall and conversion KPIs
  • Manage department store concession reconciliations, commissions and wholesale account settlements
  • Oversee stock control and valuation, including stock counts, consignment and shrinkage reporting
  • Work with production and supply chain on costings, purchase orders and supplier terms
  • Oversee EPOS, payment providers and cash handling controls across the boutiques

Transactional finance and controls

  • Oversee purchase ledger, sales ledger, credit control, expenses and supplier payment runs
  • Manage banking relationships, multi-currency accounts (including GBP, HKD, USD and EUR) and FX exposure
  • Coordinate payroll with the outsourced provider, including commissions and pensions
  • Design and maintain robust financial controls, approval processes and policies
  • Manage the overseas entity's finance with local accountants, including intercompany reconciliations

Systems, people and wider operations

  • Improve and integrate finance systems (accounting software, EPOS, e-commerce platform, inventory)
  • Drive automation and process improvement as the business scales
  • Manage and develop a small finance team (e.g. a finance assistant or bookkeeper)
  • Oversee insurance, leases, contracts and other operational and compliance matters
  • Act as a trusted adviser to the founder and wider leadership team


Requirements
Essential

  • Qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA or CIMA) or qualified by experience
  • Experience in retail, luxury, fashion, or another multi-channel consumer business
  • Proven ownership of month end, management accounts, budgeting, forecasting and year-end audit
  • Strong grasp of stock accounting, margin analysis and cash flow management
  • Hands-on experience in an SME or founder-led business, comfortable working without a large team
  • Advanced Excel skills and experience with cloud accounting software (e.g. Xero, Sage or NetSuite)
  • Confident communicator who can explain financial information clearly to non-finance colleagues

Desirable

  • Experience with department store concessions and wholesale accounts
  • Exposure to international entities, multi-currency accounting and FX
  • Knowledge of EPOS and e-commerce platforms (e.g. Shopify) and their integration with finance systems
  • Experience implementing new systems or scaling finance through a period of growth
  • Understanding of precious metal pricing, duty or import processes

Personal attributes

  • Hands-on, pragmatic and happy to roll up their sleeves
  • Commercially minded, curious and proactive in spotting improvements
  • Highly organised, with strong attention to detail and the ability to juggle priorities
  • Discreet, trustworthy and able to build strong relationships with a founder
  • Collaborative and personable, with an appreciation for a creative, brand-led culture

job.title: Interim Finance Manager
job.description:
Our client
A international luxury hospitality business. They’re looking for a hands-on Interim Finance Manager to join the London group finance team, covering management and financial reporting and technical balance-sheet accounting, with a real opportunity to move into a permanent role supporting the group’s finance transformation.

Key responsibilities

  • Own the monthly management accounts (P&L, balance sheet and cash flow) with clear commentary
  • Produce variance analysis against budget and forecast, explaining what is driving performance
  • Prepare and support statutory and financial reporting, including year-end audit files and auditor queries
  • Manage IFRS 16 lease accounting, including right-of-use assets, lease liabilities, modifications and disclosures
  • Own the PPE and fixed asset register, covering capitalisation, depreciation, impairment reviews and capex tracking
  • Account for investments, including valuations, intercompany positions and consolidation entries
  • Act as a finance business partner to operational, development and commercial teams
  • Work with property and development teams on capital projects and investment appraisals
  • Support budgeting, forecasting and board reporting packs
  • Lead balance-sheet reconciliations and clean up legacy balances
  • Strengthen month-end processes, controls and documentation
  • Support process improvement, systems and transformation projects
  • Handle ad hoc analysis and projects for the Senior Finance Director

Key requirements

  • ACA, ACCA or CIMA qualified, with solid post-qualification experience
  • Strong track record in management and financial reporting, ideally in a multi-entity or international group
  • Practical, hands-on knowledge of IFRS 16 leases, PPE and investment accounting
  • Experience of cleaning up balance sheets and improving processes
  • Hospitality, real estate, luxury or other asset-heavy sector experience is an advantage
  • Hands-on, detail-focused and organised under deadline pressure
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and keen to help shape a function in transformation
  • Confident communicator with both finance and non-finance colleagues
  • Able to work from the Central London office five days a week
